note: Static explainers for Macro Engine pillars, keyed by engine row id. Content: Hercules (COLLAB.md spec, 2026-10-08). Update `live` as conditions change.

fiscal.body: Deficits, debt sustainability, sovereign spreads. Funds stress leaks into the currency.
fiscal.live: Nov 9: NZ election — Luxon's coalition holds a paper-thin 67-seat majority (Labour won the party vote 29.36% vs 29.21%); kiwi firmed overnight; official result Nov 27. US: Democrats sweep the midterms — AP called the Senate, NBC/CBS project the House — divided government into 2027 caps the fiscal-expansion path; yields + DXY fell in Asia on the result. UK: Healey's first Budget DELIVERED Oct 28 — headroom £15B in 2029/30 (vs £23.6B March), OBR 2027 growth cut to 1.0%. France: Moody's SPARED France (Aa3 affirmed, negative outlook); Fitch cut France's outlook to negative Oct 30 (A+ affirmed; debt to ~124% of GDP by 2028 from 115.7% in 2025, deficit 5.4% in 2026) — both agencies now negative; S&P reviews Nov 27. Nov 5: Canada Budget 2026 tabled ('Masters of Our Destiny'): 2025-26 deficit C$39.3B (vs C$66.9B forecast); annual deficits C$50-60B, under 2% of GDP, over five years. NZ election preliminary count Sat Nov 7: NO clear winner — National 42 seats, Labour 36; National+ACT+NZ First hold 67 seats, a bare majority; Opportunity crosses 5% (5.9%) and enters parliament for the first time; official results Nov 27 after special votes — no government until coalition talks conclude. NZ election: preliminary count complete (99.4%) — Labour won the party vote 29.36% vs National 29.21% (3,650 votes), but National+ACT+NZ First hold 67 of 131 seats; ~399,365 special votes remain, official result Nov 27 — no government until coalition talks conclude.
fiscal.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk

growth.body: Who is accelerating, who is stalling (GDP, jobs, PMIs). Always comparative. Stronger growth pulls in capital and raises hike expectations.
growth.live: Nov 9 London: no US data today — the tape is all positioning into Tue CPI; US wholesale trade 9:00am CT + $58B 3Y auction 12:00pm CT are the only scheduled items. US Q3 GDP advance BEAT: 3.4% SAAR (vs 3.2% consensus, prev 2.2%); JOLTS BEAT 7.523M + factory orders BEAT +1.8% Nov 3; ADP BEAT (+86K vs +67K fcst) but ISM services small MISS (54.5 vs 54.8) Nov 4. Nov 5 7:30am CT triple beat: claims 189K (vs 197K fcst, matching a 57-year low), Q3 productivity +3.6% (vs 2.8%), ULC -0.7% (vs +0.3%) — into payrolls Fri (fcst +65K, unemployment 4.2%). NZ Q3 jobs MISS Nov 3: employment -0.1% (vs +0.4% fcst), unemployment 5.7% (vs 5.5%) — the week's big NZ print went the wrong way. EZ Q3 GDP BEAT (+0.4% q/q vs 0.2% fcst) but France CONTRACTED (-0.1%). Nov 6 7:30am CT: US payrolls BEAT +165K (vs 65K fcst; Sep revised to +60K, Aug to +186K), unemployment 4.1%, wages +0.4% m/m — Canada jobs MISSED (-4.7K, unemp 6.7%). Nov 6 9:00am CT: UoM sentiment BEAT 51.0 (vs 48.1 fcst); Canada Ivey PMI small beat 58.3. EZ retail sales MISSED -0.7% m/m (biggest fall since June 2024) but German IP BEAT +0.7% on autos. Nov 9: China CPI/PPI printed — CPI missed 0.7% y/y, PPI beat 5.7% (four-year high). US CPI Tue 7:30am CT (fcst +0.3% m/m, no y/y published — Oct 2025 data gap) — the last CPI before the Dec 9 FOMC; UK GDP Thu; US PPI Fri (+0.4% m/m fcst).
growth.title: Growth differentials

inflation.body: CPI/PCE vs the central bank's target. High inflation alone strengthens nothing — what matters is what the bank does about it.
inflation.live: Nov 9 London: Brent's slide to $95.16 (-3.2%) eases the energy-inflation impulse into Tuesday's US CPI; gold ~$4,121 (+1.25%) as softer oil cools inflation worries. Nov 9: China split — CPI MISSED 0.7% y/y (vs 0.8% fcst, prev 0.9%; core 0.8%) while PPI BEAT 5.7% (vs 5.3% fcst, prev 5.0%), a four-year high on higher oil prices; the CPI–PPI gap widens to ~5pp. US Sep PCE in line: headline +0.5% m/m, +3.6% y/y; core +0.3% m/m, +3.1% y/y. Swiss CPI BEAT Nov 3: +0.2% m/m, 1.5% y/y (vs 1.3% fcst). Nov 4: EZ flash CPI PRINTED inline at 4.0% (prev 3.8%, a three-year high, energy 20.8% y/y), core steady 2.5% (Reuters/Eurostat) — December ECB hike case intact. AU Q3 CPI hotter than the RBA's path (trimmed 3.7% y/y). Nov 5: Q3 ULC -0.7% (vs +0.3% fcst) — wage costs fell outright as +3.6% productivity outran +2.9% hourly compensation (BLS). Nov 6 Asia: oil's rebound fanned inflation worries, gold eased to ~$4,063 (Reuters); BoE sees UK CPI near 5% by mid-2027. Nov 6: UoM 1-yr inflation expectations cooled to 4.3% (from 4.7%; 5-yr 3.4% vs 3.5%) — household inflation fears easing into Tuesday's US CPI; EZ retail miss flags demand softening as energy bites.
inflation.title: Inflation

policy.body: Central banks moving in different directions. It is the gap between them that moves currencies: money flows toward higher rates.
policy.live: Nov 9 London: Dec Fed hike ~81% (Reuters/CME FedWatch, up from ~79% in Asia; MarketWatch 80.5%) — the payrolls beat + AI-rout pause into Tuesday's Oct CPI (7:30am CT). Williams/Musalem/Daly Fri all backed further hikes. Nov 9: Dec Fed hike ~79% (Reuters/CME FedWatch, up from 71% a week ago) — the +165K payrolls beat held through the weekend; Oct CPI Tue 7:30am CT (fcst +0.3% m/m, core +0.2%, no y/y) is the next test. FOMC HELD Oct 28 at 3.75-4.00% (10-2; Cook + Hammack for a hike) — December hike ~68% Nov 6 Asia (CME FedWatch via Reuters), ~70% into the London morning (Samuel & Co), down from ~80% Nov 5 US session and 81.2% Nov 5 morning, as the equity rout pulled yields lower; payrolls Fri 7:30am CT (fcst 65K) is the next test. RBA HIKED Nov 3 to 4.85% (6-3, fifth hike of 2026). Nov 5: BoE HIKED to 4.00% (8-1; Mann for +50bp) — first since Aug 2023; Bailey: not necessarily the last unless the Middle East conflict is resolved; CPI seen near 5% by mid-2027. ECB HELD Oct 29 at 2.50% — Dec 17 hike ~89% (Barchart/CME) after the inline Oct flash CPI (4.0%, core 2.5%); Lagarde: 'many indicators between now and December'. BoJ Dec hike ~80% (September minutes reinforced; Ueda speaks Fri 10:00am CT). Nov 6: the +165K payrolls beat re-arms the December Fed hike case (DXY 102.20); Canada's jobs miss (-4.7K, unemp 6.7%) questions the BoC's December further-hike case. Nov 6 close: Dec Fed hike ~77% (CME FedWatch, up from ~67% Thu) after the payrolls beat; Ueda: real rates 'have not risen significantly' — Dec BoJ hike ~80% intact; Lane: gather info to December, Dec ECB hike ~89%. Dec Fed hike ~76-77% holding into Tuesday's CPI (CME FedWatch ~75.5% Nov 8); BoC Dec hike faded to ~32-36% after the Canada jobs miss (swaps ~32%, OIS 36.4%) — hold now the base case.
policy.title: Policy divergence

positioning.body: Where speculators already stand (CFTC COT, Fridays). When nearly everyone has made the same bet, it can unwind fast: if everyone is long dollars, nobody is left to buy. The contrarian lens — where would a surprise hurt most.
positioning.live: Oct 27 CFTC (released Oct 30): euro net short at a 3-yr low (non-commercial -143,894; contrarian +1 — squeeze side up); yen longs at the 98th percentile (contrarian -1); AUD/NZD shorts at 1st-percentile extremes (contrarian +1 each); GBP shorts at the 5th percentile (contrarian +1); CAD read is population-mixed, held neutral. Scores moved: GBP 3->4, JPY -1->-2, AUD 2->3, NZD 3->4. Next CFTC release Fri Nov 6, 2:30pm CT — the 4pm run picks it up. Nov 3 CFTC cut released Fri 2:30pm CT — percentile scoring vs the Oct 27 cut carries to the 2am run; board scores unchanged. Nov 3 CFTC (released Nov 6): EUR net short -157,791 (5th pct of 20y, 11-yr extreme) and JPY net long +102,321 (98th pct) still crowded; GBP's short unwound (+19,593 w/w to -59,821) out of the extreme — GBP positioning score 1 → 0. AUD -129,457 and NZD -60,015 still crowded short; CAD -41,775 after heavy covering (+24,649). Next CFTC cut (Nov 10 data) due later this week.
positioning.title: Positioning

risk.body: Risk-on vs risk-off. Fear bids USD, JPY, CHF (havens) and sells AUD, NZD, GBP (risk proxies).
risk.live: Nov 9 London: the AI rout pauses — Nikkei +2.8%, Taiex +5.3%, S&P futures firmer; risk rebounds, DXY ~101.88 (-0.3-0.4%), NZD +1.0% and AUD +0.5% lead. Trump plays down new Iran strikes ('highly unlikely' while talks progress) — oil slides, the haven bid eases. Nov 9 Asia: the AI/data-center rout pauses — Nikkei +2.6%, S&P futures +0.6%; Nvidia trades tonight on the Huang admission. Haven bid eased slightly: USD/JPY ~158.28, USD/CHF ~0.8193; DXY ~102.20; AUD/NZD firmed overnight. AI/data-center rout: Nasdaq -5.5% Thursday (steepest US stock decline since April 2025) on fears of tighter scrutiny of AI data-centre construction; Asia's tech-heavy markets crumbled Friday. Haven bid went to JPY/CHF (USD/JPY one-week high 157.27, USD/CHF ~0.8171) and the dollar (DXY ~101.7), not risk: AUD weakest again (~0.6916, ~1.5% down from Wednesday's close), NZD weakest of the majors overnight. 10Y ~4.84% (lowest since Sep 10), 2Y ~4.47% in Asia (Reuters). Democrats' midterm sweep (both chambers) set up the tape: divided government into 2027, AI-regulation fears, and pressure to end the Iran war. London: dollar firmer toward 102.00 into payrolls (FXStreet); US futures trying a mild bounce; 10Y ~4.84%, 2Y ~4.48% flat in European trading (Reuters). Post-payrolls: DXY jumped to 102.20 (+0.62%) on the +165K beat; USD strongest vs NZD (-1.01%) and AUD (-0.90%) (FXStreet). Nov 6: Nasdaq bounced ~2% after Thursday's -5.5% rout (Reuters) — risk steadied into the close; the dollar, not havens, took the payrolls bid (DXY 102.33, +0.73%). Saturday: NZ election ends with no clear winner (coalition talks + Nov 27 official result); Qatar's two-day Iran proposal under review, US limited strikes Fri. Futures reopen Sun 6pm ET, Asia reopens Mon with the Nikkei in a bear market. Weekend quiet after Friday's tape; futures reopen Sun 5pm CT. Sun: IRGC lifted its self-imposed 2,000km missile-range limit (AP, Sat); Houthis hit Riyadh (Aramco Tower damaged, no supply disruption); Trump told CNN a new Iran strike is 'highly unlikely' — the diplomacy track eases the premium even as the missile signal hardens; FX closed, no price read until the 5pm CT reopen.
risk.title: Risk sentiment

tot.body: Export prices vs import prices: oil, metals. The same price moves two currencies opposite ways — say which and why.
tot.live: Nov 9 London: Brent slid to $95.16 (-3.2%, Reuters) as the Iran premium unwinds after Trump's remarks; WTI ~$90.51 (-0.4%) — Brent falls far harder than WTI, the geopolitical premium coming out of the global benchmark. Gold ~$4,121 (+1.25%) as softer oil eases inflation worries. Nov 9 Asia: Brent ~$98.3 / WTI ~$91.3 flat after a -13.3%/-11.8% week, the steepest since COVID, as diplomacy outruns supply fear — Trump says new Iran strikes 'highly unlikely'; he meets the Qatar PM today 12:00pm ET. Khor Mor drone strike Sun night halted Iraq's biggest gas field (LPG tank hit, fire doused, ~2.8 GW of Kurdish power out, no claim) — gas, not oil; no restart timeline. Brent ~$100.0 in London Nov 6 (Samuel & Co) / WTI ~$91.4 in Asia (Reuters) — a second straight gain after Thursday's +3.5%/+2.8% rebound, on Hormuz supply worries (two tankers + a tug caught fire in the Strait); still set for a ~12% weekly drop, the worst week since the post-midterm de-escalation repricing. Wednesday's crash: Brent $94.62 (-8.67%), WTI $88.12 (-8.7%) as the White House tied the midterm rout to the Iran war. Iran sent the US a nuclear proposal via Qatar; Eurasia cut Iran-deal odds to 10% (from 20%), US-attack odds to 60% (from 65%). Brent-WTI spread ~$8.3. Gold ~$4,052 in London, up ~4% on the week. Nov 6 close: Brent $98.32 / WTI $90.83 — official Friday settlements (CNBC), +$0.03/+$0.31 on the day; the morning spike above $100 faded; Brent -13.3% on the week, steepest since COVID. Gold spot ~$4,051 (Kitco 13:54 CT; Dec futures $4,074.90) as the dollar jumped. Nov 7: Iran reviewing Qatar's two-day proposal (AP) — US lifts blockade + releases some frozen funds, Iran reopens Hormuz on day 2, IAEA inspectors into bombed sites, then expanded nuclear talks; Tehran holds seven conditions before nuclear talks; Qatar PM Nov 7 'confident' a settlement can be reached; US carried out limited strikes Fri on an Iranian air-defense system. Brent $98.32 / WTI $90.83 — official Friday settlements (CNBC). Weekend: IRGC lifted its 2,000km missile-range limit (AP Sat); Houthis hit Riyadh Sun morning (Aramco Tower damaged, no supply disruption) — the Hormuz premium stays alive into the Sunday 5pm CT reopen.
